data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in GOES CCOR-1 and to the northwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no corresponding source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-30T01:48Z. The CME is also seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C3 and to the NNE in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely associated with a C3.0 flare from beyond the NE limb (~N12) that peaked at 2026-08-30T01:20Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131. Some ejecta from beyond the NE limb can also be seen in SDO AIA 304.

CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-08-30T03:24Z. It is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source may be related to some very minor field line movement near the E limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-08-30T02:00Z.

CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 and faintly to the W in STEREO A COR2, the front fades after early frames and is not visible in LASCO C3 or GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely far-sided field line movement observed beyond the E limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-08-30T09:06Z.

CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. The source is a filament eruption in the north central disk centered ~N35E05 observed in SDO AIA 304, and additionally in STEREO A EUVI 304 on the NE limb as viewed from STEREO A. The filament begins to rise as early as approximately 2026-08-29T22:00Z, rising faster after 2026-08-30T06:00Z, and fully lifts off with on-disk brightening after 2026-08-30T11:00Z. Also observed as some field line movement and dimming in SDO AIA 171/193.

This CME is visible to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is an eruption centered near S14E60 starting around 2026-08-30T16:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the southeast limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery.

CME observed to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and NE in STEREO A COR2. There is no clear EUV source for this CME, but could be slow moving and brightening field lines, and weak dimming, in the north central disk starting as early as 2026-08-30T20:00Z spanning approximately N35W05 - N35W10.

CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and in GOES CCOR-1 though somewhat obscured by earthshine. The source is likely AR 14521 associated with a C1.0 flare peaking at 2026-08-31T03:33Z observed in SDO AIA 131, with northward deflected field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193.

CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and in GOES CCOR-1 though somewhat obscured by earthshine. The source for this CME is not clear and could be related to AR 14521 as triangulation fits the front ~E70; potentially as faint loop brightening in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-08-31T04:58Z centered around N16E75 that could be sympathetic to the eruption at 2026-08-31T03:31Z associated to CME 2026-08-31T04:12Z. Some weak field line movement to the E is observed in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-08-31T04:00Z as another potential candidate.

CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is an unnumbered area of the disk centered around S13E53. At 2026-08-31T05:12Z and again at 2026-08-31T06:42Z, dimming and field line movement are observed here in SDO AIA 171/193, the latter eruption also with post-eruptive brightening.

Faint CME observed to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 and NE in STEREO A COR2. No distinct source in EUV imagery is observed, likely originating from the high latitude north central disk, with broad, slow field line movement and dimming in SDO AIA 171/193.

Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and one frame of STEREO A COR2, fading into background and weakly visible in LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is an eruption centered ~S12E68 with no active region, observed as field line movement, brightening, and dimming in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-09-01T04:24Z.

CME first seen to the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-01T21:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-09-01T19:08Z. The source of this event is a small region of dimming centered at approx. N05E50 beginning at approx. 2026-09-01T20:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 193.

Narrow CME first seen to the W in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-09-02T00:08Z. No appropriately timed source can be seen on the solar disk. There is some post-eruptive brightening from former AR 14513 (N05W105) best seen in STA EUVI beginning around 2026-09-02T00:55Z that may be related.

CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-09-02T07:24Z. It is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. The source is most likely a small eruption from an unnumbered region centered around S15E55 best seen in SDO AIA 193 beginning around 2026-09-02T05:31Z. Measurement indicates some deflection from the source region; this is consistent with the proximity to a small coronal hole centered around S00E25 at the time of the eruption.

Very faint CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-09-02T10:24Z. It is more easily seen to the E in STEREO A COR2. It is not seen in SOHO LASCO C3 or GOES CCOR-1. The source is possibly related to a minor eruption from the vicinity of AR 14522 best seen in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-09-02T09:10Z.

Bright CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap. The source of this CME is an M3.0 flare from an unnumbered region just beyond the NE limb. It is possible this is the returning region 14507 (N04) which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2026-08-21. This long duration flare is associated with visible moving/opening field lines in SDO/AIA 193, 171, 211, GOES SUVI 304 and 284 starting around 2026-09-02T19:00Z. It is also associated with a filament eruption (best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2026-09-02T19:08Z), EUV wave (best seen in SDO/AIA 193 starting around 2026-09-02T19:27Z), and post-eruptive arcades visible in SDO/AIA 193 and 171 starting around 2026-09-02T21:00Z. There may also be H-alpha emission visible within SOHO LASCO C2 & C3 imagery.

Feature first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-09-03T01:37Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNE in STEREO A COR2. This feature is likely outflow following CME: 2026-09-02T19:36Z.

Slow CME first seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-09-03T03:12Z. It is also seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. This feature is easiest to see in STEREO A COR2. The source may be related to some very faint field line movement best seen in SDO AIA 193 beginning as early as 2026-09-03T00:00Z centered around N50E40.

CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-09-03T04:48Z. It is also seen to the E in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C3. The source is likely related to wide opening field lines beyond the E limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 beginning as early as 2026-09-03T04:14Z.

CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-09-03T10:15Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and speculatively to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is a large filament eruption beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2026-09-03T09:30Z

Narrow CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-09-03T11:01Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. A possible source is a  C2.2 flare from AR 14523 (N11E44) seen peaking at 2026-09-03T09:42Z in SDO AIA 131, along with faint dimming seen in SDO AIA 193.

CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There are two possible sources. The first possible source is a slow, gradual field line loop rising/opening seen in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-09-03T14:00Z. The second potential source is a C6.9 flare from AR 14523 (N11E41) peaking at 2026-09-03T14:46Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Based on triangulation of features, it is more likely the opening field lines seen in GOES SUVI 284.

Wide, slowly billowing CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This CME overlaps and overtakes the CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-09-03T18:00Z. The source for this CME is likely moving/opening field lines visible to the NE in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-09-03T18:00Z.

CME visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely moving/opening field lines visible beyond the E limb in GOES SUVI 284. This CME partially overlaps with the CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-09-03T19:12Z.

CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this CME is a filament eruption visible to the SE in GOES SUVI 304 with associated moving/opening field lines visible in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-09-03T21:56Z.

CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME is not visible in GOES CCOR-1 due to an outage. The source is likely AR 14524 (approximately N12E63). An eruption with moving field lines starting around 2026-09-04T05:09Z is best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery. The eruption is not clearly seen in STEREO A EUV imagery.

CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-04T08:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 due to a data gap which began at 2026-09-04T03:30Z. The source of this event is filament ejecta seen along the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-09-04T08:28Z, along with field line opening seen in GOES SUVI 284.

CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The CME is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. The source is likely near the SE limb, as brightening and moving field lines are seen around S17E80 in SDO AIA 193 around 2026-09-04T12:42Z.

CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is an eruption near AR 14525, with several possible eruption candidates, including brightening and opening field lines seen starting around 2026-09-04T13:42Z.

Narrow, faint CME visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely on or just beyond the E limb, as seen by moving field lines in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA around 2026-09-04T16:00Z.

CME with an unclear leading edge visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery and there is a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 covering this event. The source for this CME may possibly be an eruption from AR 14524, however it is not clear.

Fast CME visible to the E/SE in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is a real-time DSN gap in the SOHO LASCO data covering the timing of this event. The source of this CME is a flare with associated filament eruption from AR 14524 (N12E55) starting around 2026-09-04T19:08Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304.

This CME is visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is a real-time DSN gap in the SOHO LASCO data covering the timing of this event. The source of this CME is an eruption from beyond the E/NE limb with visible deflection to the NE starting around 2026-09-04T20:52Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304.

This CME is visible to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery and SOHO LASCO C2 imagery for a few frames before becoming too diffuse to observe. The source is likely an eruption centered near S18E15 as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-09-05T05:15Z. Dimming is observed east of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193/GOES SUVI 195 imagery, indicating possible eastern deflection.

This CME is visible to the east/southeast in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 imagery in real time due to a data gap starting at 2026-09-05T03:30Z. The source is an eruption and C6.4 flare from Active Region 14524 (N12E45) starting around 2026-09-05T10:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery.

Bright CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and as a full halo in STEREO A COR2. The source is associated with an M1.0 flare from AR 14520 peaking at 2026-09-05T15:18Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. The eruption is additionally observed as field line movement, wide EUV wave, dimming, filament ejecta, and post-eruptive arcade/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193/211/304 starting at 2026-09-05T15:04Z. Observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 as brightening at 2026-09-05T15:15Z and STEREO A EUVI 195 as dimming at 2026-09-05T15:55Z.

This CME is visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is related to an eruption and C8.5 flare from Active Region 14524 (N12E42) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and GOES SUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-09-05T17:40Z. Dimming is observed south of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193/GOES SUVI 195 imagery.

Narrow CME first seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-09-05T22:00Z. It is also seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely a filament eruption near the E limb best seen in SDO AIA 304 starting around 2026-09-05T21:15Z.

This CME is visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. This event is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 in real-time due to data gaps starting around 2026-09-06T03:30Z. The source is likely related to an eruption from Active Region 14524 (N12E34) starting around 2026-09-06T06:55Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery.

This CME is visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. This event is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 in real-time due to data gaps starting around 2026-09-06T03:30Z. The source is an eruption and C5.0 flare from Active Region 14524 (N12E32) starting around 2026-09-06T10:36Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. An EUV wave and subsequent dimming is observed moving south of the eruption site, seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery.

This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is far-sided and likely related to an opening of field lines visible over the eastern limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery starting around 2026-09-07T00:50Z.

This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 (partially obscured by the pylon), and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a slow-to-lift-off filament eruption visible over the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171/304 and GOES SUVI 171/284/304 imagery starting around 2026-09-06T22:00Z. This same filament is visible lifting off north of disk center as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to an eruption from Active Region 14524 (N12E22) starting around 2026-09-07T08:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. Dimming is observed north of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 imagery, with an opening of field lines visible over the northeast limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery, indicating northern deflection.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a C2.4 flare from Active Region 14521 (N10W35) starting around 2026-09-08T12:19Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery.

Faint, narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. It is not clearly seen in available GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source of this CME appears to be a filament eruption best seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 and 195 as well as GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2026-09-09T06:52Z. There is a dimming signature visible in STEREO A EUVI 195 that appears to "pinch" towards the filament before it lifts off.

This CME is faintly seen to the East in STEREO A COR2 imagery. It appears to be associated with a C3.4 flare (caught in GOES-S) peaking at 2026-09-09T09:08Z (occurs during an eclipse in GOES-P) from AR 14524 (N15W05). This CME is very slow and not clearly seen in the SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a simultaneous CME visible to the East in SOHO LASCO C2 around the same time, however this CME is believed to be associated with a slow farsided filament eruption and is not the same CME feature seen in STEREO A that is associated with this entry.

This CME is visible to the East in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A imagery. The source of this CME appears to be a long-duration filament eruption visible along the E/SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 and 284 imagery starting around 2026-09-09T06:30Z with liftoff around 2026-09-09T10:36Z. Moving/opening field lines are visible with some apparent deflection towards the north as it progresses out of the field of view in GOES SUVI 284. The CME also exhibits a small deflection towards the north as it progresses outward in the SOHO LASCO field of view. There is a simultaneous CME visible to the East in STEREO A COR2 around the same start time, however this CME is believed to be associated with a C-class flare and is not the same CME feature seen in SOHO LASCO C2 that is associated with this entry. The CME is visible in later frames in STEREO A as a wider feature.

Wide, faint CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is also visible to the SE in STEREO A COR2 imagery, and overlaps in the field of view with CME: 2026-09-09T16:09Z. The potential source is unclear, but may be brightening and field line movement seen in the vicinity of AR 14521 (N09W48) beginning at approx. 2026-09-09T14:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 193.

Slow, wide CME visible as a partial halo to the east in STEREO A COR2. Also visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is likely field line opening and brightening seen along the East limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approximately 2026-09-09T15:00Z.

Faint CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and to the SE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is a filament eruption located around W30 to W50 stretching between longitudes S10 to S20 based on SDO/AIA 193 imagery. This eruption starts around 2026-09-10T03:00Z with filament liftoff around 2026-09-10T04:00Z as seen in SDO/AIA 193 and 304. Dimming is also visible to SDO/AIA 193.

Bright loop CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-10T20:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is not visible in GOES CCOR-1 as it is obscured by the pylon. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen near N50W120 in STEREO A EUVI 304, as well as to the NNW by GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-09-10T19:15Z. Field line opening is also visible in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284.

CME faintly seen to the SE in GOES CCOR-1 and possibly faintly in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C2 and may be obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. The potential source may be field line movement seen near the SE limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting around 2026-09-10T20:04Z.

Faint CME first seen to the NNW beginning at 2026-09-10T23:36Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is faint field line movement seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-09-10T23:00Z.

CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME is not visible in GOES CCOR-1 due to Earthshine. The potential source may be an eruption seen near the NW limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195 around 2026-09-11T02:55Z as post-eruption arcades.

CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME is not visible in GOES CCOR-1 due to Earthshine. The potential source may be near the NW limb as seen from STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. A possible eruption with moving field lines can be seen around 2026-09-11T04:25Z. The CME overlaps in the field of view with the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-09-11T05:36Z.

CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery and is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. The potential source may be an eruption from AR 14521 (N09W77) in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-09-11T11:52Z, best seen as moving field lines.

Faint, narrow CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-11T16:12Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. The source of this event is a very minor filament eruption seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 304 beginning at approx. 2026-09-11T15:00Z.

CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-13T19:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-09-13T19:23Z. The source of this event is a center disk filament eruption beginning at approx. 2026-09-13T18:48Z best seen in SDO AIA and STEREO A COR2 304, centered at approx. S10W10. This filament appears to be deflected towards the NW, which is supported by dimming seen moving towards the NW, expanding to approx. N10W30 as seen in SDO AIA 193. This eruption is close to a large coronal hole which may contribute to the deflection.

Faint CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-13T21:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-09-13T19:23Z. The source of this CME is likely outflow following an earlier filament eruption beginning at 2026-09-13T18:48Z centered at approx. S10W10 as seen in SDO AIA 193 and 304. This CME is likely deflected to the NW due to proximity to a large coronal hole.

CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-09-14T11:08Z. It is also seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1. This CME is covered by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real time. The source of this CME is an eruption centered around AR 14528 (S11W38) best seen in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2026-09-14T10:00Z. Field line movement can be seen accompanied by brightening and ejecta. Post-eruptive arcades can also be seen in SDO AIA 193. There seems to be a northwestward deflection from the location of the source. There are two large coronal holes (a northern and a southern one) nearby, possibly responsible for this deflection.

CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, likely not observed in STEREO A COR2 either due to faintness or a data gap starting at 2026-09-14T18:53Z before it becomes visible. The source is far-sided over the NW limb, observed in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-09-17T15:48Z as slow, wide field line movement. More directly observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting as early as 2026-09-14T14:55Z, as brightening and dimming centered around an estimated N30W115 in the NW disk near former Active Regions 14523 and 14521.

Faint, narrow CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 and very faintly seen in a couple of frames of GOES CCOR-1 coronagraph imagery. The CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C3. Its source is likely seen in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery as a large ejecta off the W limb after 2026-09-19T15Z and not seen in any other EUV imagery. The ejecta is not clearly visible, and it's exact location/longitude is unclear, but it seems to be close to the limb (which would be ~159 deg).

Faint, minor CME with an unclear front seen to the E-NE in SOHO LASCO C2. Not seen in other coronagraphs. Its source is the long duration C3.3 class flare from unnumbered AR rotating onto disk (N14E90) peaking at 2026-09-19T18:17Z. There is also an associated opening of field lines on/behind the E limb seen in SDO AIA 193 and a minor prominence/ejecta seen in SDO AIA 304/171 starting after 2026-09-19T18:10Z. The initial front is followed by a series of outflows.

CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is a far-sided filament eruption over the NW limb, observed best in GOES 284/304 starting around 2026-09-19T21:22Z. When STEREO A EUVI 304/195 return from a data gap at 2026-09-20T00:15Z and 2026-09-20T00:25 respectively, dimming and post eruptive brightening can be seen in the NW disk, likely left behind by this filament eruption.
CME observed brightly to the SW in STEREO A COR2, and very faintly to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No source is seen in on-disk EUV imagery for this event, and is likely far-sided.

Faint CME observed to the NW in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3, not in GOES CCOR-1 as it is likely obscured by the pylon. The only potential source is a slow brightening on the NW disk of STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-09-20T18:55Z.

Faint CME observed to the NW in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3, largely blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source is unclear, with a potential far-sided source on the STEREO A EUVI 195/304 west limb observed as brightening and field line movement starting around 2026-09-21T09:05Z, very close to the CME start time however. There are two additional field line movements near the NW limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-09-21T03:03Z and 2026-09-21T05:54Z, however these eruptions may be too early to be associated with this CME. Triangulation of the leading edge suggests the CME is far-sided.

CME observed to the E only in STEREO A COR2, likely not seen in other coronagraphs due to the occulting disk and/or faint leading edge. The start time of 2026-09-24T02:53Z in white light is later than the first observation at 2026-09-24T01:38Z in running difference imagery due to the bright streamer overlap. The source may be an eruption from AR 14536 centered around N03W32, observed as slow dimming, brightening, and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-09-23T21:06Z. In STEREO A COR2, there is a faint leading edge observed already far in the east field-of-view after a data gap ends at 2026-09-24T01:23Z that better corresponds to this eruption time, but is also plausible to be a candidate source for this CME.

CME observed to the SW in GOES CCOR-1 and S in STEREO A COR2, overlapping with a slow, wide streamer blowout beginning ~2026-09-23T20:12Z (itself measuring ~176 km/s). Not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a real-time data gap. The source is field line movement and small shifting of a coronal hole boundary best observed only in GOES SUVI 284 starting ~2026-09-24T14:02Z, tracing on-disk around S35W70 in proximity to a large southern coronal hole.

CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is also visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is farsided, and is best seen as rapidly opening field lines beyond the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2026-09-25T10:25Z. Moving field lines are also visible beyond the east limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA.

Narrow CME with a pointy front seen in STEREO A COR2 only. This CME partially overlaps in coronagraphs with the far-sided 2026-09-25T11:09Z CME and its shock. The only potential candidate source is a filament liftoff faintly seen to the south in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting 2026-09-25T11Z as a faint dimming and faint post-eruptive arcades centered ~S40W80 or W90. Not really seen in GOES SUVI 304 or STEREO A 304 imagery.

Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-26T00:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. There is no clear source for this event as it is likely far sided.

Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-26T02:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is obscured by Earthshine in GOES CCOR-1. There is no clear source seen for this event as it is likely far sided.

Bright lightbulb-shaped CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. Its source is a large prominence seen lifting from behind the SW limb starting at 2026-09-26T18:28Z (best seen in GOES SUVI 304), with source location seen on disk, close to the SW limb in STEREO A EUV 304/195 imagery. In EUV A 195 imagery we see an ejecta, as well as dimming and bright post-eruptive arcades. The erupting filament is also seen in AIA 171 and faintly in AIA 304, and ejecta and opening of field lines are seen off/close behind the SW limb in GOES SUVI 286. The erupting filament stretches very approximately from ~S25W15 (mostly dimming) to ~S20W80 (ejecta and post-eruptive arcades), as seen from STEREO A perspective, so the filament can be estimated as centered very approximately at ~S20W135 from the SDO perspective.

CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-27T06:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small eruption from the vicinity of AR 14534 (N10W95) beginning at approx. 2026-09-27T04:30Z in STEREO A EUVI 195. This CME is likely deflected to the West by a large coronal hole in the vicinity of the eruption.

CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-27T07:00Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is minor field line movement and brightening seen located at approx. S30W100-120 beginning at 2026-09-27T06:00Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195.

Narrow CME first seen to the NNE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-27T09:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1 and to the North by STEREO A COR2. There is no clear source seen for this event as it is likely far sided.

Narrow CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-28T01:26Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is an eruption seen along the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-09-28T01:00Z.

Faint CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-28T04:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. There is no clear source seen for this event.

Narrow CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-28T04:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is faint field line opening seen along the SW limb (approx. W140) in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning at approx. 2026-09-28T03:35Z.

Bright loop CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-28T14:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, as well as to the East in STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a very large filament eruption seen stretching from approx. S10W50 to N45W50 (centered at approx. N27W50) with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-09-28T13:51Z as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Post eruptive arcades, dimming and wide field line opening can be seen in SDO AIA 171/193/211, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195.
